item.title: Pearls finish on a high, but World Cup dream ends in Tonga
item.description: Fiji produced one of its strongest performances of the tournament, taking control early and heading into half-time with a commanding 32–16 lead. The Pearls maintained their composure after the break, continuing to apply pressure and eventually sealing a 21-goal victory.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji produced one of its strongest performances of the tournament, taking control early and heading into half-time with a commanding 32–16 lead.

The Pearls maintained their composure after the break, continuing to apply pressure and eventually sealing a 21-goal victory.

The result provided a positive finish to Fiji’s campaign, but it was not enough to keep their Netball World Cup hopes alive.

Tonga and Samoa secured the two qualifying places from the Oceania region and will now turn their attention to the Netball World Cup in Australia in 2027.

For the Pearls, the road to the next major tournament begins again from here.

item.title: 20-year-old Ba defender Isimeli Gavidi earns first Bula Boys cap
item.description: At just 20, Ba defender Isimeli Gavidi has earned his first senior international cap after being handed a starting role for the Bula Boys against Solomon Islands in the MSG Prime Minister’s Cup. The Ba defender started for Fiji in their opening match of the MSG Prime Minister’s Cup against Solomon Islands at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva on Friday night.
item.content:encoded:
At just 20, Ba defender Isimeli Gavidi has earned his first senior international cap after being handed a starting role for the Bula Boys against Solomon Islands in the MSG Prime Minister’s Cup.

The Ba defender started for Fiji in their opening match of the MSG Prime Minister’s Cup against Solomon Islands at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva on Friday night.

Gavidi’s debut comes after progressing through Fiji’s age-group teams before establishing himself at domestic level with Ba.

The young defender shared the field with experienced internationals, including captain Roy Krishna, as Fiji and Solomon Islands played out an entertaining 3-all draw.

The appearance marks Gavidi’s first senior international cap and gives him an opportunity to build on his progress as he looks to establish himself in the Bula Boys squad.

item.title: Skipper Cup round 8 set for another exciting day
item.description: With the business end of the season approaching, every point will be crucial as teams look to strengthen their positions on the table and build momentum heading into the remaining rounds. In the feature match of the round, unbeaten Nadi will host Nadroga at King Charles Park in what promises to be a highly anticipated Western derby.
item.content:encoded:
With the business end of the season approaching, every point will be crucial as teams look to strengthen their positions on the table and build momentum heading into the remaining rounds.

In the feature match of the round, unbeaten Nadi will host Nadroga at King Charles Park in what promises to be a highly anticipated Western derby.

Nadi comes into the match following an impressive 57–36 victory over Ba last weekend, while Nadroga will be looking to build on its 31–22 win over Malolo.

At 4R Stadium in Ba, Ba will welcome Naitasiri in another important encounter.

Both sides will be determined to bounce back and make their mark after contrasting results in Round 7.

Suva will take on Malolo at the Suva Grammar School Ground, with the capital side aiming to turn its recent form into another positive result.

Suva played out a 17–17 draw with Lautoka last weekend, while Malolo went down 31–22 to Nadroga.

At Ratu Cakobau Park in Nausori, Tailevu will face Lautoka.

Tailevu will enter the contest with confidence after defeating Kadavu 30–10 in Round 7, while Lautoka will be looking to improve after sharing the points with Suva.

Rewa will host Navosa at the Burebasaga Grounds, while Taveuni will meet Kadavu on the Garden Island.

Taveuni narrowly lost 35–31 to Rewa last weekend, while Kadavu suffered a 30–10 defeat against Tailevu.

All six matches are expected to provide another competitive afternoon of provincial rugby, with teams knowing that the results could have a significant impact as the Skipper Cup race continues.

The Round 8 matches kick off at 3pm, except for the Nadi–Nadroga clash, which starts at 3.30pm.

item.title: Crocodile-infested river cleared to host Brisbane 2032 Olympic rowing events
item.description: A river that is home to around 500 saltwater crocodiles has been given the go-ahead to host Olympic and Paralympic rowing and canoeing events at the 2032 Brisbane Games. The course on the Fitzroy River in Rockhampton, Queensland, has passed an independent technical assessment of its suitability.
item.content:encoded:
A river that is home to around 500 saltwater crocodiles has been given the go-ahead to host Olympic and Paralympic rowing and canoeing events at the 2032 Brisbane Games.

The course on the Fitzroy River in Rockhampton, Queensland, has passed an independent technical assessment of its suitability.

The assessment did not consider the crocodiles, but instead examined "how the course would perform under a range of conditions, weather patterns, water levels and flood risk at both games time and throughout the period leading into the games.

The report was commissioned by the Games Independent Infrastructure and Coordination Authority (GIICA), which noted that the Fitzroy River Flatwater Facility "is already a training and competition venue for flatwater sports, supporting school state championships, local regattas , and national team training camps.

As an established rowing facility, contingency plans are in place for events when crocodiles are spotted, and Olympic officials have previously been assured that rowers can compete safely.

World Rowing and Paddle Worldwide, formerly the International Canoe Federation, have both endorsed the course.

Rowing President Jean-Christophe Rolland says b ased on the extensive analysis undertaken, they now know that the Fitzroy River is capable of providing fair competition conditions during the period of the Games, consistent with the requirements of Olympic and Paralympic Rowing.

Brisbane 2032 President Andrew Liveris played down concerns about crocodiles last year.

He says there are sharks in the ocean and they are still surfing, it's a can-do, not a can't-do – please change the mindset here.

Saltwater crocodiles, known locally as salties, live in both freshwater and saltwater and can grow to more than six metres in length.

Drew Ginn, who won three Olympic gold medals for Australia in rowing, told BBC Radio that he has concerns about potential flooding and "fairness and integrity" at the venue, as well as the Olympic experience for athletes and spectators at a location "six or seven hours" from Brisbane.

Gin sa ys personally, he is not fearful of the Australian animals, but he never had a crocodile near him.

He says all the athletes would row faster knowing whats beneath the waters.
